For a mail server, that isn't a super easy setup. Usually you need two things at a minimum: an SMTP service and an IMAP/POP service. The SMTP service deals with the actual sending and receiving between mail servers. The IMAP/POP service lets you read mail on the server or download it using an email client. I personally prefer Postfix and Dovecot to do these. If you want a webmail interface, there's a number of them but Roundcube seems to be a good one. It requires a webserver (Apache, PHP, MySQL) to run.

If you want a free solution that does cloud storage I would recommend OwnCloud. For the web interface it requires a webserver (same as above) but you can also get free desktop clients for all platforms. If you spend $10 you can get an SSL certificate from Name.com or NameCheap and then the connections get encrypted for additional security.
Thanks for your reply. Is there that letsencrypt a possibilty for an ssl certificate? Or is that something else entirely?

I believe that a certificate from the LetsEncrypt initiative would be fine. If not, I've actually done it with a self-signed certificate. You get warnings that it is an invalid certificate and that there is a security risk if you don't know who generated the key and csr/crt, but if you do it yourself then there's no security risk.

The first thing you have to find out is if your ISP allows traffic on the ports used for email, because a lot don't; 110 for pop3 and 25 for SMTP, IMAP is 465 I think, there are others depending on your need for security.

You also need a static IP address, which some ISPs don't provide. I'm talking residential ISPs here.

If neither of those are an issue then what you describe is certainly doable but, and it's a big but, requires a fair amount of knowledge AND especially in the case of a mail server is generally more work to set up and maintain than is worth it. It's a great learning exercise though.

The other thing you'll need is a good firewall and the ability to route traffic on your internal network. If you decide to add a web server then you'll need to create a DMZ for it.

iRedMail is a pretty good open source email solution with a web I/F, and it includes AV and spam. As mail servers go installation is pretty straightforward BUT you'll need a decent understanding of the basics beforehand.

As captbrogers mentioned OwnCloud is excellent for a cloud server.

For server admin there's a nifty tool called Webmin that you should look into.

I have no comment on that router. Security is your #1 concern though, and 2nd you need the ability to direct certain traffic to the addr of the server. A domain name is convenient but not necessary because you can always just use the outward facing IP address, bit of a PITA though.

I forgot to mention that the modem your ISP gave you needs to support pass through mode. This is why security is so important; you're essentially opening your internal network to the world.
